newsitem.title: USA: Chase to use Mondex in smart card test.
newsitem.headline: Chase to use Mondex in smart card test.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp will switch to the Mondex technology for stored value cards in a pilot program in New York city which has now been delayed until the fourth quarter of 1997, a news release from particpants said Wednesday.

The announcement noted that under the original plan Chase Manhattan was going to use MasterCard Cash. Last month MasterCard, one of the two big U.S. credit card associations, said it would buy a 51 percent stake in Mondex, which is mostly owned by a large group of international banks.
The original launch date for the pilot, which will be closely watched by the U.S. banking industry, was the first quarter of 1997.
As originally planned, Citicorp's Citibank unit will issue cards using Visa's own independently developed stored value product, VISA Cash, for the program.
The stored value cards are popularly known as smart cards.
It is expected that 500 merchants will accept the cards, the announcement said.
